newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Overseas investment in Shenzhen rises 40 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Overseas investment in Shenzhen rises 40 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Overseas investment in China's southern boomtown of Shenzhen rose 39.59 percent year-on-year to a record US$2.422 billion in 1996, the Shenzhen Special Zone Daily said on Friday.
As of end-1996, the accumulated foreign investment in the city had topped US$11.8 billion channelled into about 18,000 projects, the newspaper said.
Hong Kong remained the biggest investor last year, but combined investment from the territory, Macau and Taiwan saw a decline of about 30 percent, the newspaper said.
South Korean firms became the second biggest foreign investors in Shenzhen, pumping in a total of US$509 million, it said.
Of the 999 overseas-funded projects approved by the Shenzhen government in 1996, 858 were industrial projects, including 29 each with an investment of at least US$10 million, it said.
